hero.lead: An island nation of 1.24 million with $10.3 billion of reserves, which has set itself a legal anchor to bring public debt of 87.8% of GDP down to 75% by 2030.

stats.label: Public sector debt, share of GDP, 2025/26

capital.heading: Rich in reserves, heavy in debt, anchored by law.

record.text: Public sector gross debt, share of GDP, 2025/26; the Budget 2026/27 framework projects 85.6% in 2026/27 and 79.8% in 2028/29
Fiscal anchor in law: public sector debt of 75% of GDP by end-June 2030, Public Debt Management Act as amended in 2025
Government expenditure in the Budget 2026/27, presented on 19 June 2026, against revenue of Rs 235.5 billion and an estimated deficit of Rs 31.2 billion
Budget deficit target, share of GDP, 2026/27, after 6.0% in 2025/26 and 9.3% in 2024/25

register.name: National Budget 2026/27
register.detail: Presented 19 June 2026 · expenditure Rs 266.7 billion · revenue Rs 235.5 billion · deficit Rs 31.2 billion, 3.7% of GDP
register.note: Government spending in the year to June 2027
register.text: Includes about Rs 10.6 billion of receipts from the Chagos agreement. It pays for the public services behind all seven standards.

register.name: Rodrigues Airport Project
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 29 September 2023 · project P180266
register.note: Principal of US$184,000,000, as listed by the World Bank Group
register.text: An IBRD loan to the Republic of Mauritius for the Rodrigues Airport Project, approved on 29 September 2023. Better air links for the island of Rodrigues serve the livelihood standard, through visitors and trade with the main island.

register.name: Gas Insulated Switchgear Substations Project
register.detail: African Development Bank · Approved July 2023 · named on 19 January 2024 as a beneficiary of the Room to Run Sovereign programme, with the United Kingdom
register.note: Total project cost $110 million; the loan amount is not stated in the release
register.text: Expands the grid to connect variable renewable energy and make supply more reliable, with an estimated 133 MW of solar PV to be connected to new and refurbished substations. It supports the national target of 60% renewable energy in electricity generation by 2030, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Special Economic Package: grant-cum-line of credit projects
register.detail: Government of India · Joint Announcement, 11 September 2025 · EXIM Bank of India tender for Motorway M4, 27 February 2026
register.note: Approximately USD 440 million (MUR 20.10 billion), the estimated cost of the four projects
register.text: Grant and line of credit finance for the new air traffic control tower at SSR International Airport, Motorway M4, Ring Road Phase II and port equipment for the Cargo Handling Corporation. Roads, the airport and the port serve the livelihood standard, through trade and jobs.

register.name: Special Economic Package: grant projects
register.detail: Government of India · Joint Announcement, 11 September 2025 · grant basis
register.note: Approximately USD 215 million (MUR 9.80 billion); USD 25 million of budget support also agreed in principle for the same financial year
register.text: Grants for a new Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam National Hospital, an AYUSH Centre of Excellence, a Veterinary School and Animal Hospital, and helicopters. The new national hospital serves the health standard.

register.name: Green credit line to SBM, backed by the Green Climate Fund
register.detail: AFD · Signed April 2025, during the official visit of the French Minister for Francophonie and International Partnerships · Transforming Financial Systems for Climate programme
register.note: With a €1.2 million technical assistance grant; one of six agreements worth nearly €160 million
register.text: A green credit line for renewable energy, energy efficiency and the circular economy, backed by the Green Climate Fund. It gives a Mauritian bank long-term money for clean power, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Green credit line to MauBank, backed by the Green Climate Fund
register.detail: AFD · Signed April 2025, during the official visit of the French Minister for Francophonie and International Partnerships · Transforming Financial Systems for Climate programme
register.note: With a €1.2 million technical assistance grant; one of six agreements worth nearly €160 million
register.text: A green credit line for renewable energy, energy efficiency and the circular economy, backed by the Green Climate Fund. It gives a Mauritian bank long-term money for clean power, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: MCB climate finance facility
register.detail: Proparco, DEG and FMO · Announced 1 April 2026 · senior loan arranged by Proparco under the Friendship Facility · equal commitments
register.note: For climate projects in Mauritius and across Africa; the share for Mauritius is not stated
register.text: A senior loan to the Mauritius Commercial Bank that will primarily finance renewable energy projects, with the possibility to support climate adaptation, in line with its Sustainable Finance Framework. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Stor’Sun I to IV, solar and battery storage
register.detail: Qair · Announced 19 February 2026 · SBM Bank (Stor’Sun I, II and IV) and MCB (Stor’Sun III) · 100 MWp of solar with 256 MWh of battery storage
register.note: Approximately USD 150 million; the largest energy project financing in Mauritius in a decade, according to Qair
register.text: Bank financing for four plants that combine solar power with battery storage. Once operational, they will supply 8% of national electricity demand and reduce reliance on fossil fuels, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Absa Mauritius climate credit line
register.detail: Proparco · Signed 15 October 2024 · senior credit line fully dedicated to the climate
register.note: About 14,000 indirect jobs to be supported over five years in the companies the bank finances
register.text: A senior credit line to Absa Bank (Mauritius), with nearly all the funds for climate mitigation projects. It serves the energy standard and, through the firms it finances, livelihood.

register.name: Accelerating the transformational shift to a low-carbon economy in the Republic of Mauritius (FP033)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · accredited entity UNDP · single-country project
register.note: The amount and approval date are not shown on the Green Climate Fund country page
register.text: The single-country Green Climate Fund project for Mauritius, under implementation with UNDP, to accelerate the shift to a low-carbon economy. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: MCB syndicated term loan
register.detail: Closed February 2026 · syndicated term loan · banks from the Gulf and India
register.note: Funding raised by The Mauritius Commercial Bank
register.text: Medium-term funding for The Mauritius Commercial Bank, which lends to firms and households. It serves Livelihood.

register.name: Accelerating the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive economy in Mauritius
register.detail: Start 23 May 2025 · GEF-8 · full-size project · GEF ID 11087 · UNEP
register.text: Helps Mauritius move to a low-carbon economy that protects nature. It serves Energy and Livelihood.

register.name: UK–Mauritius agreement on the Chagos Archipelago, including Diego Garcia
register.detail: Signed 22 May 2025 · treaty · 99 years · net present value £3.4 billion, verified by the Government Actuary’s Department
register.text: Recognises Mauritian sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago while the United Kingdom keeps the Diego Garcia base. The payments go to the budget that pays for the seven standards.

register.name: Economic Competitiveness and Resilience Support Program, Phase II
register.detail: Approved 22 May 2024, Abidjan · budget support loan · fisheries law, an agriculture and livestock roadmap 2024 to 2030, rooftop solar for lower-income households
register.text: Budget support tied to reforms in fisheries, farming and household solar. It serves Food, Energy and Livelihood.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Reserves
items.label: Gross international reserves, 2025
items.text: Reserves worth about two thirds of a year’s output: a base for long-term finance in local currency.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Cane fields that built the economy, ready to be priced as land, energy and food.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Cane, sun and water already give a fifth of the power.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: FoodWise
items.text: A social enterprise founded in 2018 that makes food donation a tool against food waste. Since 2018 it has enabled the redistribution of more than 8 million meals; in May 2026 it launched a pact for tax relief on food donations, signed by 24 major agri-food players.

items.name: Zardin La Laura
items.text: A family farm at La Laura, Saint-Pierre, founded in 2021 with one hydroponic greenhouse, now run with connected sensors, artificial intelligence, automation and precision agriculture. It grows more than 25 varieties of vegetables, fruit and herbs on over 5,300 m² of protected crops, producing more than 3,500 kg a month.

items.name: Happynest
items.text: A start-up answering the housing crisis with modular tiny houses on a certified steel frame, faster to build and more affordable than traditional construction. It won the Rising Star and Power Pitch awards at the Turbine Innovation Challenge in October 2025.

items.name: YUVA Academy
items.text: A social enterprise of the youth organisation YUVA, registered with the Mauritius Qualifications Authority as a training institution, with schools of leadership, entrepreneurship, humanities and robotics and remedial classes for secondary-school learners in Port Louis. Its revenue-generating courses help sustain YUVA’s community work.

items.name: TIBOK (Digital Data Solution)
items.text: A telemedicine platform based in Grand Baie that uses clinical artificial intelligence and offers consultations seven days a week, e-prescriptions, connected pharmacies and same-day delivery; it states that it is fully operational across Mauritius and Rodrigues. Employers pay Rs200 per employee per month for its welfare programme.
